agentCan: Implement the authorization-code flow, host-aware API calls, and rotating-refresh persistence
Prepare app values (name, redirect URIs, scope list)

approval.cost: None: 'Usage of our API is completely free', allowed on any plan including Free
approval.trigger: None described. The official developer docs contain no app review, approval queue, or marketplace listing process for API Apps: registration is self-serve in the portal and users can authorize immediately. No user caps before approval are stated (there is no approval).

blockers.detail: API base URL differs per user's data center (US or EU). Using the wrong host returns 401 'Access token is unknown or invalid'. Always build API URLs from the host value in the token response.
blockers.howToClear: Read host from every token response and route that user's calls to https://<host>/api/v4.
blockers.title: The host trap

blockers.detail: 'The refresh operation returns a new access token and a new refresh token, making the old refresh token invalid.' Clients must persist the replacement every time or strand the connection.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the new refresh token atomically on every refresh.
blockers.title: Refresh-token rotation

blockers.detail: The App Console offers a Permanent Access Token ('Get token', shown only once) that never expires and grants full account access. The FAQ warns permanent tokens 'are not intended to be used in multi-user applications'. It is a dead end for a SaaS, fine only for testing or single-user tools.
blockers.howToClear: Use the OAuth flow for anything multi-user; reserve permanent tokens for internal testing.
blockers.title: Permanent Access Token trap

sources.label: OAuth 2.0 authorization (flow, host, rotation, token lifetimes)
FAQ (free API, permanent token warning, consent cannot be scripted)

tested: Read-only verification: app registration, the authorization-code flow, host behavior, rotation, and the absence of any review were checked against current developers.wrike.com pages (no app created, nothing submitted)
unverified: Whether creating an API App requires an account-admin role (not stated in the docs read).
The full scope catalog (docs give per-method requirements and examples; no single enumerated list found).
Whether an app registered in one Wrike account can be authorized by users of unrelated accounts, in those exact terms (docs describe consent generically and per-account data access).

alternatives: Permanent Access Token (per-user, never expires, full account access; explicitly not for multi-user applications)
flavor.recommended: A Wrike API application (API App) in the Apps & Integrations portal / App Console, standard authorization-code flow (the only flow Wrike supports)
flavor.why: Registration assigns a Client ID and Client Secret. 'Wrike API requests are executed on behalf of the end-user, who gives consent for the third-party app through OAuth2 protocol.' There is no client-credentials or daemon flavor.

humanMust: Be a Wrike user and create the API App in the portal
Run the initial consent (the FAQ is explicit it 'cannot be fully scripted or run with cURL')
name: Wrike
nuances: Tokens die with the user: OAuth and permanent tokens are revoked when the user revokes manually, resets their password, is deactivated, an admin uses 'Log in as this user', or an admin changes the password-strength policy (the last invalidates tokens even when the user's password already complies).

One account at a time: API v4 'can access data from only one account at a time'; multi-account users pick an account on an extra consent screen. The app sees only what the authorizing user can see under Wrike's sharing settings.
Redirect URIs must be HTTPS; http://localhost is allowed for development.

Scopes are requested per authorization call (comma-delimited, case-sensitive), not fixed at registration; each API method's doc lists its required scopes. Docs recommend requesting only necessary scopes.
Rate limit is approximately 400 requests per minute (per-second based), with 429 + exponential backoff guidance.
For UI-less/background apps the docs suggest a dedicated 'technical' user, with a manual browser consent run first.
prerequisites: A Wrike account (any plan, including Free)
Redirect URI(s) (HTTPS; localhost allowed for dev)

steps.detail: Any Wrike user can do this ('API use is completely free and allowed for accounts with any subscription plan').
steps.title: Sign in as a Wrike user

steps.detail: Create the app in the portal; note the Client ID and Client Secret; register your redirect URI(s) (HTTPS; http://localhost allowed for development).
steps.title: Create the API App; register redirect URIs

steps.detail: GET login.wrike.com/oauth2/authorize/v4 with client_id, response_type=code, and optional redirect_uri, state, and scope (comma-delimited, case-sensitive). The user logs in, consents, and picks an account if they belong to several. The code is valid 10 minutes.
steps.title: Send the user to the authorize URL

steps.detail: POST to login.wrike.com/oauth2/token with client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code, code. The response carries the access token, refresh token, expires_in 3600, and the host value.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: Call https://<host>/api/v4 with the token in the Authorization header; the host comes from the token response because data sits in US or EU data centers. Refresh via the token endpoint (host-specific base URL) with grant_type=refresh_token; every refresh returns a NEW refresh token and invalidates the old one.
steps.title: Call the API at the returned host; handle rotation

tagline: Self-serve OAuth with no review at all. The difficulty is mechanical: every token response carries the data-center host your calls must use, and every refresh rotates the refresh token and kills the old one.

time.active: ~15 min of portal setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Same day; no approval stands in front of users
